questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : Min-max normalization is useful when data boundaries are known and fixed.
S2 : Z-score is suitable when the data follows a Gaussian distribution.
Which of the above statement is correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• Min-max normalization rescales data to a fixed range (commonly [0, 1]).
It is most useful when minimum and maximum boundaries are known and stable, such as in image pixel normalization. So, S1 is correct.
• Z-score normalization standardizes data to have mean = 0 and standard deviation = 1.
It assumes data is approximately normally distributed (bell-shaped) for effectiveness in tasks
like PCA or statistical analysis. So, S2 is correct.

questions.qtext: Consider a relation S = (A, B, C, D). For which of the following sets of FD’s in S is not in 3rd normal form?

options.text: {ABC → D, ACD → B, A → D, BCD → A}
{AD → C, BC → A, BD → C, CD → B}
{AC → D, D → A, D → B, D → C}
{AC → B, A → D, C → A, D → B}

questions.solution:
(d)
For (i): For FD A → D, the LHS is not the super key but RHS is a prime attribute. Therefore, it is
in 3NF.
For (ii): The candidate keys are AD, BD and CD. Thus, for FD BC → A, the LHS is not the
superkey but RHS is a prime attribute. Therefore, it is in 3NF.
For (iii), The candidate keys are AC and D. Thus, all the FD's satisfy the 3NF condition and thus
it is in 3NF.
For (iv), the candidate key is C, therefore, FD AC → B, A → D, D → B neither LHS is the super
key nor RHS is having the prime attribute, therefore, it is not in 3NF.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : Equal-width binning divides the range of data into fixed-size intervals, while equal-frequency binning adjusts interval size to balance record count.
S2 : Equal-width binning is range-based, whereas equal-frequency binning is count-based.
Which of the above statement is correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• Equal-width binning divides the total data range into fixed-size bins, while equal-frequency
binning adapts bin widths to ensure equal number of records per bin. So, S1 is correct.
• Equal-width binning is based on the range of data, while equal-frequency binning is based on
maintaining the same number of records in each bin. So, S2 is correct.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct?

options.text: Equal frequency discretization always ensures bins of equal width.
Min-max normalization may distort data relationships if outliers are present.
A fact table in a star schema contains quantitative data and foreign keys to dimension tables.
In a star schema, dimension tables are connected hierarchically before linking to the fact table.

questions.solution:
(b, c)
• Equal frequency discretization creates bins with an equal number of data points, not equalwidth
ranges. Bin widths may vary based on data distribution. So, option (a) is incorrect.
• Min-max normalization uses extreme values (min and max) for scaling, so outliers can skew
the transformation, compressing the majority of data. So, option (b) is correct.
• A fact table contains measurable numerical data (facts) and foreign keys referencing the
associated dimension tables in a star schema. So, option (c) is correct.
• That describes a snowflake schema. In a star schema, each dimension table connects directly
to the central fact table without hierarchy. So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.qtext:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : In a Fact Constellation schema, dimension tables are shared among multiple fact tables.
S2 : In a Star Schema, dimension tables are shared among multiple fact tables.
S3 : In a Snowflake Schema, dimension tables are shared among multiple fact tables.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(a)
• Fact Constellation supports multiple fact tables sharing common dimension tables.
It is suitable for complex systems involving interrelated subjects. So, S1 is correct.
• In Star Schema, each fact table has its own dimension tables.
Dimension tables are not typically shared across multiple fact tables. So, S2 is incorrect.
• Snowflake Schema normalizes dimension tables into sub-tables for optimization.
It does not imply sharing of dimension tables between fact tables. So, S3 is incorrect.

questions.qtext: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.text: Drill-down provides insight into specific trends by unfolding summarized information.
Pivot operation reduces data volume by aggregating facts into higher levels.
Roll-up uses random grouping of data without considering dimension hierarchies.

questions.solution:
(a)
• Drill-down increases data granularity by navigating from higher to lower levels in a hierarchy.
It helps analyze finer details hidden under aggregated summaries. So, option (a) is correct
• Pivot operation rearranges the orientation of dimensions for alternative views.
It does not perform aggregation or reduce data volume like roll-up. So, option (b) is incorrect
• Roll-up aggregates data using well-defined concept hierarchies, not random groupings.
This structured hierarchy guides summarization from detailed to general levels. So, option (c)
is incorrect.

questions.qtext: Which of the following is/are correct?

options.text: MLOP identifies the most frequently taken path and leverages this for future predictions,improving accuracy for stable branching behavior.
ROLP gives higher accuracy than MLOP in irregular branch scenarios because it relies on the most recent path taken.
MLOP typically requires maintaining frequency counts or path statistics, leading to higher storage overhead compared to ROLP.
Both MLOP and ROLP are inherently compatible with two-level global branch history predictors without any conflict.

questions.solution:
(a, b, c)
• MLOP tracks the most frequently taken execution path to enhance prediction reliability.
This approach improves accuracy for branches with consistent and stable behavior. So, option (a)
is correct.
• ROLP focuses on the most recently observed path, adapting quickly to changes.
Hence, it performs better in scenarios with irregular or dynamic control flow. So, option (b)
is correct.
• MLOP maintains path frequency statistics, which requires additional counters.
This leads to a higher storage overhead compared to ROLP's minimal tracking. So, option (c)
is correct.
• MLOP and ROLP are not inherently conflict-free with two-level global predictors.
Integration can cause aliasing or interference depending on indexing and history length.
So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.qtext:
Consider a relation R(A, B, C, D, E, F) with the following functional dependencies.
{AB → C, C → D, AF → B, B → E}
Which of the following is/are true?

options.text: Relation is in 2NF, but not in 3NF.
{B → E} is a partial dependency, so relation violates 2NF.
The FD : {C → D} violates BCNF, as C is not a super key.
Replacing {C → D} with {AB → D} and keeping all other FD’s, make the relation BCNF complaint.

questions.solution:
(a, c)
AF is the only candidate key.
• No partial dependency exist, so relation is in 2NF.
• There exist transitive dependency from AF → B → E hence relation is not in 3NF.
• Replacing FD : {C → D} with {AB → D} do not make relation in BCNF.
